Local Man Transforms Into Corn, Visits South Dakota's Famed Corn Palace

Officials are asking the public to remain calm — and, under no circumstances, attempt to harvest the individual.

By KORN 12 News Desk  ·  Special Report  ·  4:27 PM CT

MITCHELL, SOUTH DAKOTA — In what experts are calling one of the strangest agricultural developments in recent memory, a local man has reportedly undergone a complete transformation into an ear of corn, making an appearance outside the world-famous Corn Palace.

Witnesses described the individual as approximately six feet tall, dressed in a navy-blue blazer, and possessing an unusually large number of golden-yellow kernels. Authorities confirmed that the individual appeared to retain his original facial features, including his eyes, nose, and distinctive salt-and-pepper goatee.

The man appeared to be in stable condition and showed no apparent signs of distress.

“I'm just happy to finally be somewhere I belong.”

The transformation has sparked considerable interest among local residents and tourists, many of whom have traveled to the Corn Palace specifically to witness the unusual visitor.

Corn Palace officials have yet to issue a formal statement, though sources suggest the facility may be considering offering the individual an honorary membership.

Agricultural specialists remain baffled. Early speculation points to an undiscovered biological phenomenon, an unusually aggressive case of seasonal allergies, or prolonged exposure to excessive amounts of corn.

When asked whether he intended to return to his previous human form, the man reportedly declined to comment.

Instead, he simply stared into the distance.

And smiled.

This is a developing fictional story. More information will be provided as it becomes available.
